title: Practice: Reactions of Acids with Metal Oxides

questions.stem: Copper oxide reacts with sulfuric acid to produce a blue solution. What is the balanced equation for this reaction?
questions.explanation: Metal oxide + acid -> salt + water. CuO + H2SO4 -> CuSO4 + H2O. The blue solution is copper sulfate. Note there is no hydrogen gas produced (unlike metal + acid reactions). Option B shows a metal reacting with acid; Option D incorrectly includes hydrogen gas.

questions.stem: When black copper oxide powder is added to warm dilute hydrochloric acid, what observations would you expect?

options.text: Fizzing occurs and a brown solid forms
The black powder dissolves and the solution turns green/blue, with no gas produced
The solution turns red and gas is given off

questions.explanation: The black copper oxide dissolves in the acid as it reacts: CuO + 2HCl -> CuCl2 + H2O. Copper chloride solution is green/blue. No gas is produced because this is an oxide-acid reaction (producing salt + water only), not a metal-acid reaction. The black powder gradually disappears as it dissolves.

questions.stem: Why are metal oxide + acid reactions classified as neutralisation reactions?

options.text: Because a base (metal oxide) reacts with an acid to form a salt and water
Because they always produce a pH of exactly 7

questions.explanation: Neutralisation is the reaction between an acid and a base to form a salt and water. Metal oxides are bases (they react with acids to form salt + water). For example, CuO + H2SO4 -> CuSO4 + H2O follows the pattern: base + acid -> salt + water. The oxide ions in the metal oxide accept H+ ions from the acid.

questions.stem: A student wants to make zinc chloride salt from zinc oxide and hydrochloric acid. She adds excess zinc oxide to the acid. After the reaction, how should she obtain pure zinc chloride crystals?

options.text: Evaporate all the water immediately over a strong flame
Filter off the excess zinc oxide, then gently evaporate the filtrate to form crystals
Add more acid to dissolve all the zinc oxide
Cool the mixture and scrape off the crystals

questions.explanation: Excess zinc oxide ensures all the acid has reacted. The unreacted zinc oxide is removed by filtration (it is insoluble). The filtrate contains pure zinc chloride solution. Gentle evaporation (or evaporating to the point of crystallisation, then cooling) produces pure zinc chloride crystals. Rapid boiling could decompose the salt or cause spitting.

questions.stem: Iron(III) oxide reacts with nitric acid. What are the products?
questions.explanation: Metal oxide + acid -> salt + water. The salt name depends on the acid: nitric acid (HNO3) produces nitrates. So Fe2O3 + 6HNO3 -> 2Fe(NO3)3 + 3H2O. The products are iron(III) nitrate and water. No hydrogen gas is produced in metal oxide reactions with acids.
